  <div class="project-card">
    <h3>Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness in DeepSeek R1</h3>
    <div class="badge-row">
      <span class="badge badge-type-research">Research &amp; Publication</span>
      <span class="badge badge-status-complete">Complete</span>
    </div>
    <div class="skill-tags">Python · LLM evaluation · Prompt design · Statistical analysis</div>
    <p>MSc thesis examining whether DeepSeek R1's stated reasoning actually reflects the factors driving its answers.</p>
    <details>
      <summary>Details</summary>
      <p>Found that the model would change its final answer in response to a hint embedded in the prompt, without ever mentioning that hint anywhere in its chain-of-thought. Published in the ACL Anthology as part of IJCNLP-AACL 2025, CHOMPS workshop.</p>
      <a href="https://aclanthology.org/2025.chomps-main.2/" target="_blank">Read the paper →</a>
    </details>
  </div>

  <div class="project-card">
    <h3>Meal Planner</h3>
    <div class="badge-row">
      <span class="badge badge-type-personal">Personal Project</span>
      <span class="badge badge-status-complete">Completed</span>
    </div>
    <div class="skill-tags">LLM, web scraping, data processing, UI/UX</div>
    <p>A meal planning system, it scrapes recipes from the web, uses a local LLM to tag them, scales portions, and generates a weekly plan that tries to balance season, effort and variety.</p>
    <details>
      <summary>Details</summary>
      <p>Solving a niggle, 500 recipes were scraped from the web, processed, tagged using a locally-hosted LLM, and a weekly plan can then be generated with regards to season, effort, diet requirements, etc. A local version is also available that allows users to customise for the size of their household, and rate recipes (per individual).</p>
      <a href="meal_planner.qmd">Read more here</a>
    </details>
